description:
About the Fellowship

The NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP) is America's most graduate fellowship for STEM fields, including all engineering disciplines. This fellowship supports outstanding graduate students in NSF-supported science, technology, engineering, and mathematics disciplines who are pursuing research-based master's and doctoral degrees.

Funding & Benefits

  • Stipend: $37,000 per year (2026-27 rate) for 3 years
  • Cost of Education Allowance: $16,000 per year to institution for 3 years
  • Professional Development: XSEDE supercomputer access, international research opportunities
  • Total Value: Approximately $159,000 over 3 years

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Citizenship: U.S. citizens, nationals, or permanent residents
  • Academic Standing: College seniors, first-year graduate students, or those pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees
  • Field: Engineering, Computer Science, or related STEM field
  • GPA: Typically 3.0+ (though competitive applicants usually have 3.5+)

Application Process

  1. Register and create profile.
  2. Prepare application.
  3. Submit by deadline.
  4. NSF evaluation.
  5. Award notification.
  6. Begin fellowship.

Required Components

  • Personal Statement: 3-page essay describing background and career goals
  • Graduate Research Plan Statement: 2-page research proposal
  • Three Letters of Reference: From academic or research supervisors
  • Transcripts: All undergraduate and graduate records
  • Test Scores: GRE (optional for 2027 but recommended)

Timeline & Deadlines

StageDate
Application OpensSeptember 2026
Engineering DeadlineOctober 2026 (typically late October)
Review PeriodNovember 2026 - February 2027
Award NotificationApril 2027
Fellowship StartFall 2027

Official Link

https://www.nsfgrfp.org/

Important Notes

  • Most STEM fellowship in the United States.
  • Allows you to choose any research topic and any accredited U.S. institution.
  • Access to supercomputing resources and international research opportunities.
  • NSF fellows have high success rates in academic and industrial careers.
  • Frame engineering research as addressing societal challenges while demonstrating technical excellence.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: Field-specific deadlines (8:00 PM Eastern): 19 October 2026 — Life Sciences; 20 October — Computing, Materials, Psychology and Social Sciences; 22 October — Engineering; 23 October — Chemistry, Geosciences, Mathematics, Physics and Astronomy. References: 16 October 2026.. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

Open the official application page ↗
